Dr. M.S. Swaminathan's
recommendations on agricultural
sector
*261. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that agricultural
scientist, Dr. M.S. Swaminathan has come
out with a report containing far reaching
recommendations for achieving high growth
in agriculture and making the farm produce
competitive;
(b) whether the recommended
agricultural reforms envisage massive
investment in the agricultural sector by both
the public and private sectors; and
(c) if so,  the details of these
recommendations and Government's policy
thereon?
Prime Minister's Japan visit
*262. SHRI RUMANDLA RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL  AFFAIRS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Prime Minister's visit to
Japan has been successful;
(b) if so, whether Japan has agreed to
provide aid that was stopped due to the
Pokhran test;
(c) to what extent Japanese investment
in India would increase; and
(d) if so, to what extent these agreements
would help?
Amendment to Industrial Disputes
Act, 1947
*263. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of LABOUR
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-report captioned
"Central labours to make lay-offs easy"
which appeared in the 'Newstime' dated the
23rd February, 2002; and
(b) the safeguards taken/proposed to be
taken to protect interests of labour before
amending the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
to lay off employees without Government's
permission?

Ban on duplicate brands of goods
†*264. SHRI RAJNATH SINGH
'SURYA': Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the companies making
consumer goods are demanding for a special
ban to check the duplicate brands of the
goods;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the present laws are not
effective; and
(d) the steps Government propose to take
in the matter?
Council for Clean India
*265. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central
Vigilance Commission has formed a Council
for Clean India (CFCI);
(b) if so, what is its composition and
objectives;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the Central
Vigilance Commission (CVC) is coming
up with a new measurable index for
Government organisations called as
"Corruption Permission Index"; and
(d) if so, the definition of the Index?
Use of IT in SSI sector
*266. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of SMALL SCALE
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Small Scale
Industry is much backward so far as
application of Information Technology is
concerned;
(b) whether the SSI is lacking in
productivity, cost control and
competitiveness in the absence of
Information Technology;
(c) if so, whether Government propose
to give incentives to the SSI with a view to
help them in inducting Information
Technology; and
(d) if so, the details of the steps taken/
being taken by Government in this
regard?
Uniform sugarcane price
*267. SHRI NARENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD  AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for not having uniform
sugarcane price all over the country as
sugarcane itself is a major cost input in
manufacturing sugar; and
(b) if not, the administrative difficulties
in doing so?
FBI Director's Delhi visit
*268. DR. KARAN SINGH: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether following the Home
Minister's US visit, the Director
Investigation of the Federal Bureau of
Investigations of the US, Mr. Robert
Mueller visited New Delhi;
(b) if so, the purpose of the visit and the
outcome thereof; and
(c) the nature and extent of cooperation
to fight terrorism expected to be extended
by the FBI?

Allotment of rice at BPL rates
*269. DR. (MS.) P. SELVIE DAS: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to allot five kg. rice per head per month at
BPL rates in addition to the States BPL
Quota to destitute children, schools for
physically handicapped, old age houses and
other related institutions sponsored by the
State Governments;
(b) if so, whether the Government of
Karnataka has requested to allocate 6000
MT rice at the BPL rates; and
(c) if so, the action taken by Government
in this regard?
Foodgrain stocks
*270. PROF. A. LAKSHMISAGAR:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD  AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the buffer stock position of
foodgrains at the end of 2001 and
procurement target during 2002;
(b) the estimated loss of foodgrains
during 2001 in comparison to the loss
during 1999;
(c) whether Government have
considered the possibility of the existing
food security system to manage storage of
foodgrains in the warehouses;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether any change in the
procurement and distribution policy is
contemplated by Government to minimise
the annual losses of foodgrains; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
International support to Pakistan on
Kashmir issue
*271. SHRI C.M. IBRAHIM: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken note
of the fact that on January 4th, 2002, when
Pakistan's spokesperson announced from
Kathmandu that struggle of Kashmiris for
implementation of the UN Security Council
resolutions, recognizing right of the people
of Jammu and Kashmir for self
determination, was their indigenous
movement and could by no stretch of
imagination be called terrorism, the British
Prime Minister from Bangalore and the U.S.
Defence Secretary of State from Washington
supported Pak-position as strong; and
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto
to set the international scenario in right
perspective?
Financial information on terrorism
funding
*272. PROF. M. SANKARALINGAM:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have recently,
discussed with USA about sharing financial
information to crack down on terrorism
funding;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the merits and demerits of such an
understanding with USA?

†*273. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(e) if not, what action Government
propose to initiate against the persons
involved in issuing these uniforms?
National Highway Patrol Force
*274. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government would consider
constituting a special National Highway
Patrol Force, comprising both of Civil Wing
and Law Enforcement Wing under the
National Highway Authority of India;
(b) whether Government consider such
a step necessary due to increasing
lawlessness on National Highways and also
to remove blockades caused by accidents/
encroachments etc.; and
(c) whether it is also proposed to include
para-medical personnel in the Patrol Force
to provide first-aid treatment to accident
victims?
Cottage industries in rural areas
*275. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
announce new incentives to encourage

(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

CHANDRA KHARWAR:
SHRI VIJAY SINGH YADAV:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some officers

Unnao;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that some
officers have refused to join their new duties

functioning of communication system there;
and
(d) if so, what is the justification for
their not joining the new duties and what
action is being taken by Government against
the officers?

new operators
*277. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that "Spectrum

Telecom facility in hilly and tribal
areas

DUGGAL: Will the Minister of

steps to provide/improve telecom services

(b) if so, the details thereof, district-wise?
Opposition to labour reforms
legislation
*280. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO: Will the Minister of LABOUR be
pleased to state:

(c) whether they are against the
disinvestment of Blue Chip Public Sector
